title: TypeScript, OOP, Decorators, and Webpack
subtitle: Comprehensive reviewer for Modules 1 to 6 covering TypeScript basics, classes, decorators, Webpack, ITL rules, and advanced types.

questions.t: What causes a dynamic typing runtime error in JavaScript?
choices: Invoking a number method on a string variable.
Declaring a constant variable without a value.
Importing a module that contains private data.
Running code inside an outdated browser engine.
questions.a: Invoking a number method on a string variable.

questions.t: What happens when you read the value property of a numeric HTML input in JavaScript?
choices: The browser returns the value as a plain text string.
The browser converts the value into a floating number.
The browser returns null until the user presses enter.
The browser triggers an automatic type check failure.
questions.a: The browser returns the value as a plain text string.

questions.t: What does the exclamation mark operator (!) do when placed after a DOM selector query?
choices: It asserts to the compiler that the returned node is not null.
It converts the selected HTML element into an active listener.
It forces the browser engine to search for the element again.
It resets all existing property values on that DOM component.
questions.a: It asserts to the compiler that the returned node is not null.

questions.t: What does the as HTMLInputElement type assertion do in TypeScript?
choices: It informs the compiler of the specific DOM element type.
It creates a new HTML input element in active memory.
It parses the inner text content of the element as JSON.
It converts the element structure into a plain data array.
questions.a: It informs the compiler of the specific DOM element type.

questions.t: What does the unary plus operator (+) do when placed before a string value?
choices: It converts the string value into a number.
It creates a copy of the input DOM element.
It checks if the string contains any text.
It logs the element value into the console.
questions.a: It converts the string value into a number.

questions.t: How does a transpiler differ from a standard compiler?
choices: It outputs code in another high-level language instead of machine code.
It converts source files directly into binary instructions for the CPU.
It bundles external package dependencies into one single output script.
It executes the written source program inside memory without compiling.
questions.a: It outputs code in another high-level language instead of machine code.

questions.t: Why cannot web browsers execute TypeScript files directly?
choices: Web browsers only understand and run standard JavaScript syntax.
Web browsers require all files to be compiled into binary code.
Web browsers block all strongly typed files for security reasons.
Web browsers only load scripts that come from an external domain.
questions.a: Web browsers only understand and run standard JavaScript syntax.

questions.t: What does TypeScript do when you initialize a variable with a value?
choices: It automatically infers the data type from that initial value.
It converts the variable into a universal dynamic any structure.
It creates a global interface definition for that single item.
It prevents the variable from holding any future assigned value.
questions.a: It automatically infers the data type from that initial value.

questions.t: What does the void return type signify on a TypeScript function?
choices: It indicates that the function returns no value.
It forces the function to return a null pointer.
It converts any returned result into an integer.
It prevents the function from taking parameters.
questions.a: It indicates that the function returns no value.

questions.t: How does the unknown type differ from the any type in TypeScript?
choices: It requires you to narrow or check the type before using the value.
It allows you to invoke arbitrary methods without prior validation.
It converts any assigned primitive into an immutable object shape.
It disables all static type checks across the entire project file.
questions.a: It requires you to narrow or check the type before using the value.

questions.t: What is the primary function of a union type in TypeScript?
choices: It allows a single variable to store several specified types.
It merges two separate class definitions into one constructor.
It converts an array of numbers into a fixed tuple structure.
It creates an immutable copy of an existing interface contract.
questions.a: It allows a single variable to store several specified types.

questions.t: What does a literal type do in TypeScript?
choices: It restricts a variable to an exact, specific value.
It allows a variable to accept any primitive number.
It converts a string variable into an integer literal.
It forces an object to inherit properties from another.
questions.a: It restricts a variable to an exact, specific value.

questions.t: What is one key difference between an interface and a type alias?
choices: Interfaces support declaration merging while type aliases do not.
Type aliases accept method signatures while interfaces reject them.
Interfaces only store primitives while type aliases handle objects.
Type aliases allow class implementation while interfaces forbid it.
questions.a: Interfaces support declaration merging while type aliases do not.

questions.t: What is the effect of placing a question mark (?) after an interface property name?
choices: It marks the property as optional during type validation.
It prevents the property from being assigned a null value.
It converts the property into a private internal variable.
It forces the property to receive a default initial string.
questions.a: It marks the property as optional during type validation.

questions.t: What is the default numeric value of the first member in an unassigned enum?
choices: It starts at the numeric value 0.
It starts at the numeric value 1.
It defaults to an empty string.
It requires an explicit number.
questions.a: It starts at the numeric value 0.

questions.t: What is the main benefit of using string enums in TypeScript?
choices: They eliminate magic strings and group related constants together.
They allow functions to take an unlimited number of arguments.
They convert client-side scripts into compiled machine binaries.
They execute code in the browser without requiring transpilation.
questions.a: They eliminate magic strings and group related constants together.

questions.t: In TypeScript, this operator (!) asserts to the compiler that a value returned from a query is guaranteed not to be null or undefined.
questions.a: non-null assertion operator

questions.t: This keyword in TypeScript is used to define custom type aliases for unions, primitives, or object shapes.
questions.a: type

questions.t: This TypeScript keyword defines an object contract that can be implemented by classes and supports declaration merging.
questions.a: interface

questions.t: This type-safe alternative to 'any' requires developers to narrow or verify data types before performing operations on the value.
questions.a: unknown

questions.t: Web browsers can execute TypeScript (.ts) files directly without any transpilation.
questions.a: False

questions.t: In TypeScript, a function with a return type of 'void' does not return any value to the caller.
questions.a: True

questions.t: List three core primitive data types supported in TypeScript.
How does JavaScript resolve a property lookup on an object?
choices: It searches the object and then moves up the prototype chain.
It queries the global namespace before checking local fields.
It inspects all child classes before reading current instance.
It converts all inherited methods into static class functions.
questions.a: It searches the object and then moves up the prototype chain.

questions.t: What does the hasOwnProperty() method check on an object?
choices: It checks if a property belongs directly to that object instance.
It deletes inherited prototype methods from the current instance.
It copies all prototype fields into a brand new object instance.
It prevents external code from adding properties to that instance.
questions.a: It checks if a property belongs directly to that object instance.

questions.t: What is one limitation of vanilla ES6 classes compared to TypeScript classes?
choices: They lack built-in access modifiers to restrict property scope.
They cannot use constructor functions during object creation.
They prevent developers from creating multiple class instances.
They do not allow methods to return numeric or string values.
questions.a: They lack built-in access modifiers to restrict property scope.

questions.t: Which scope rule applies to a private member in a TypeScript class?
choices: It is accessible only from within the declaring class body.
It is accessible within the class and all derived subclasses.
It is accessible from any external script importing the file.
It is accessible only through static helper factory methods.
questions.a: It is accessible only from within the declaring class body.

questions.t: Which scope rule applies to a protected member in a TypeScript class?
choices: It is accessible within the declaring class and its subclasses.
It is accessible from any external function outside the class.
It is accessible only inside the top constructor declaration.
It is accessible exclusively by static utility class methods.
questions.a: It is accessible within the declaring class and its subclasses.

questions.t: What effect does the readonly modifier have on a class property?
choices: It prevents reassignment of the field after initialization.
It hides the property from being viewed in subclass methods.
It converts the property value into an immutable static enum.
It restricts property access exclusively to private getters.
questions.a: It prevents reassignment of the field after initialization.

questions.t: How does constructor parameter property shorthand work in TypeScript?
choices: It declares and assigns class fields directly in parameters.
It converts all incoming constructor arguments into strings.
It generates automatic getter and setter accessors for fields.
It prevents the class from accepting any optional arguments.
questions.a: It declares and assigns class fields directly in parameters.

questions.t: What happens when a TypeScript class implements an interface?
choices: The class must define every property and method in the contract.
The class automatically inherits method bodies from that source.
The class cannot declare any extra methods outside the contract.
The class converts all interface fields into private properties.
questions.a: The class must define every property and method in the contract.

questions.t: This keyword in TypeScript is used by a class to adopt and satisfy the contract of an interface.
questions.a: implements

questions.t: This visibility modifier makes a class property accessible only within the declaring class and any derived child classes.
questions.a: protected

questions.t: This property modifier prevents a class field from being changed or reassigned after its initial declaration.
questions.a: readonly

questions.t: List the three visibility access modifiers available in TypeScript classes.
In TypeScript classes, all properties and methods are public by default unless an access modifier is specified.
questions.a: True

questions.t: When does a TypeScript decorator function execute?
choices: It runs once when the class is defined and loaded into memory.
It runs every time a new instance of the class is constructed.
It runs only when an attached method gets called by a caller.
It runs after all child subclass constructors finish execution.
questions.a: It runs once when the class is defined and loaded into memory.

questions.t: Which group contains valid attachment targets for TypeScript decorators?
choices: Classes, methods, accessors, properties, and parameters.
Interfaces, type aliases, enums, unions, and modules.
Import statements, export clauses, packages, and files.
HTML elements, CSS selectors, script tags, and forms.
questions.a: Classes, methods, accessors, properties, and parameters.

questions.t: What happens when a class decorator modifies constructor.prototype?
choices: It attaches properties directly to the class prototype object.
It deletes existing properties from every created class instance.
It stops the class constructor from executing when instantiated.
It converts all class methods into private static declarations.
questions.a: It attaches properties directly to the class prototype object.

questions.t: What is the purpose of a decorator factory in TypeScript?
choices: It returns a decorator function while accepting custom arguments.
It creates multiple instances of a class in a separate thread.
It converts standard ES6 classes into plain prototype objects.
It bundles all module dependencies into a single output file.
questions.a: It returns a decorator function while accepting custom arguments.

questions.t: This character prefix is placed immediately before a decorator function name when decorating a target in TypeScript.
This type of higher-order function takes custom configuration parameters and returns an active decorator function.
questions.a: decorator factory

questions.t: TypeScript decorators execute each time a new instance of a class is created using the 'new' keyword.
questions.a: False

questions.t: List the 5 attachment targets for TypeScript decorators.
What is the execution order when a script imports ES modules?
choices: The imported dependency modules execute before the main script.
The main importing script executes before any imported module.
All modules execute concurrently without any defined sequence.
The browser waits for user interaction before running modules.
questions.a: The imported dependency modules execute before the main script.

questions.t: Why do browser-based ES modules require a local web server to run?
choices: Browser security policies block module imports using file protocols.
Web browsers cannot parse JavaScript files without server headers.
Local file paths prevent the browser from minifying script bundles.
TypeScript files must be compiled dynamically on the remote server.
questions.a: Browser security policies block module imports using file protocols.

questions.t: Which command creates a new default tsconfig.json file in a project?
choices: Run the command tsc --init in the terminal.
Run the command npm init -y in the terminal.
Run the command git init in the root folder.
Run the command webpack build in the shell.
questions.a: Run the command tsc --init in the terminal.

questions.t: What do the outDir and rootDir options configure in tsconfig.json?
choices: outDir specifies compiled output and rootDir specifies source files.
outDir specifies source files and rootDir specifies compiled output.
outDir includes package dependencies and rootDir sets node modules.
outDir defines dev server paths and rootDir holds the static HTML.
questions.a: outDir specifies compiled output and rootDir specifies source files.

questions.t: What problem occurs when loading many separate JavaScript files in HTML?
choices: It causes excessive network requests and fragile script ordering.
It forces the browser engine to disable all modern CSS features.
It converts local variable declarations into global window names.
It blocks the DOM from rendering any static text on the screen.
questions.a: It causes excessive network requests and fragile script ordering.

questions.t: Which 5 packages are required to set up Webpack with TypeScript?
choices: webpack, webpack-cli, webpack-dev-server, typescript, and ts-loader.
webpack, webpack-core, ts-node, typescript, and lite-server.
webpack-cli, babel-loader, typescript, parcel, and webpack-server.
webpack, typescript, ts-lint, dev-server, and browser-sync.
questions.a: webpack, webpack-cli, webpack-dev-server, typescript, and ts-loader.

questions.t: What is the role of ts-loader in a Webpack build pipeline?
choices: It transpiles TypeScript files into JavaScript during bundling.
It provides a local development server with hot module reload.
It minifies external CSS files into a single production sheet.
It creates sourcemap files for debugging inside the terminal.
questions.a: It transpiles TypeScript files into JavaScript during bundling.

questions.t: What does the resolve.extensions setting do in a Webpack configuration?
choices: It allows developers to leave out file extensions in import paths.
It automatically renames all compiled bundle files in the output.
It converts legacy CommonJS modules into modern ECMAScript files.
It prevents Webpack from processing files inside the src directory.
questions.a: It allows developers to leave out file extensions in import paths.

questions.t: This Webpack loader package is responsible for transpiling TypeScript source files into JavaScript.
questions.a: ts-loader

questions.t: This configuration file is used by the TypeScript compiler to set compiler options like outDir and rootDir.
questions.a: tsconfig.json

questions.t: This HTML script tag attribute is required when loading standard ES modules directly in the browser.
questions.a: type="module"

questions.t: List the 5 core npm packages installed for a Webpack TypeScript build setup.
Webpack combines multiple TypeScript files and dependencies into a single output bundle to reduce HTTP requests.
questions.a: True

questions.t: Which naming convention is required for classes and interfaces under ITL guidelines?
choices: Use PascalCase for class and interface names.
Use camelCase for class and interface names.
Use snake_case for class and interface names.
Use kebab-case for class and interface names.
questions.a: Use PascalCase for class and interface names.

questions.t: Which naming convention is required for enum members under ITL guidelines?
choices: Use CAPITALIZED_SNAKE_CASE for all enum member fields.
Use lower_snake_case for all enum member fields.
Use standard camelCase for all enum member fields.
Use strict PascalCase for all enum member fields.
questions.a: Use CAPITALIZED_SNAKE_CASE for all enum member fields.

questions.t: Which naming convention applies to functions, methods, and variables under ITL guidelines?
choices: Use camelCase for function names and variable identifiers.
Use PascalCase for function names and variable identifiers.
Use snake_case for function names and variable identifiers.
Use kebab-case for function names and variable identifiers.
questions.a: Use camelCase for function names and variable identifiers.

questions.t: Which naming convention applies to files, folders, and HTML id attributes under ITL guidelines?
choices: Use snake_case for all files, folders, and HTML IDs.
Use PascalCase for all files, folders, and HTML IDs.
Use camelCase for all files, folders, and HTML IDs.
Use kebab-case for all files, folders, and HTML IDs.
questions.a: Use snake_case for all files, folders, and HTML IDs.

questions.t: Which practice aligns with DLSU-D ITL TypeScript conventions?
choices: Always use curly braces when importing named components.
Include the dot js file extension on all Webpack imports.
Use the any type whenever variable types are uncertain.
Commit the node modules directory to the Git repository.
questions.a: Always use curly braces when importing named components.

questions.t: What is the standard format for a TODO comment in a TypeScript file under ITL guidelines?
choices: // TODO(Lastname, Givenname): What needs to be done
// NOTE(Lastname, Givenname): What needs to be done
<!-- TODO(Lastname, Givenname): What needs to be done -->
// TASK(Lastname, Givenname): What needs to be done
questions.a: // TODO(Lastname, Givenname): What needs to be done

questions.t: Under DLSU-D ITL conventions, CSS class names must be formatted using this naming convention.
questions.a: kebab-case

questions.t: Under DLSU-D ITL conventions, enum member names must follow this uppercase naming style.
questions.a: CAPITALIZED_SNAKE_CASE

questions.t: Under ITL guidelines, the node_modules folder should always be excluded using a .gitignore file.
questions.a: True

questions.t: Under ITL guidelines, you should explicitly include the .js extension when importing TypeScript modules with Webpack.
questions.a: False

questions.t: Where does the JavaScript prototype chain end during a property lookup?
choices: It terminates at Object.prototype which points to null.
It terminates at Function.prototype in the memory heap.
It loops indefinitely until the browser stops execution.
It resets back to the initial instance calling context.
questions.a: It terminates at Object.prototype which points to null.

questions.t: How do subclasses pass parameters to a parent class constructor in TypeScript?
choices: They invoke the super keyword with required arguments.
They call the parent class name directly as a method.
They assign values to this before invoking the parent.
They use the extends keyword inside the method block.
questions.a: They invoke the super keyword with required arguments.

questions.t: What do getter and setter accessors do in a TypeScript class?
choices: They intercept and control reads and writes to private fields.
They convert regular class methods into static background tasks.
They automatically save object states to local browser storage.
They force all numeric variables to round to the nearest whole.
questions.a: They intercept and control reads and writes to private fields.

questions.t: What is a key characteristic of an abstract class in TypeScript?
choices: It cannot be instantiated directly and serves as a base class.
It prevents derived subclasses from adding any new methods.
It allows all defined methods to run without implementation.
It converts all instance fields into public global variables.
questions.a: It cannot be instantiated directly and serves as a base class.

questions.t: What is the syntax difference between default imports and named imports?
choices: Named imports require curly braces while default imports do not.
Default imports require curly braces while named imports do not.
Named imports only import types while default imports load code.
Default imports allow multiple values while named imports take one.
questions.a: Named imports require curly braces while default imports do not.

questions.t: What does the Partial<T> utility type do in TypeScript?
choices: It transforms every property in the type into an optional field.
It makes every property in the type completely immutable to edits.
It extracts a specific subset of selected keys from the object.
It removes a specific group of unwanted keys from the contract.
questions.a: It transforms every property in the type into an optional field.

questions.t: What does the Readonly<T> utility type do in TypeScript?
choices: It makes all properties in the type immutable and read-only.
It makes all properties in the type optional during assignment.
It creates a new type containing only primitive data fields.
It removes all method signatures from an interface contract.
questions.a: It makes all properties in the type immutable and read-only.

questions.t: What does the Omit<T, K> utility type do in TypeScript?
choices: It constructs a type by removing specified keys from an object.
It constructs a type by making all keys read-only and immutable.
It extracts only the specified keys while dropping all others.
It makes all properties optional across the target interface.
questions.a: It constructs a type by removing specified keys from an object.

questions.t: This utility type constructs a type with all properties of T set to optional.
questions.a: Partial<T>

questions.t: This utility type constructs a type by picking only the specified set of keys K from type T.
questions.a: Pick<T, K>

questions.t: This keyword is used to declare a base class that cannot be instantiated directly and must be subclassed.
questions.a: abstract

questions.t: List four common built-in TypeScript utility types used to transform object shapes.
Abstract classes in TypeScript can be instantiated directly using the new keyword.
questions.a: False
